decisions.reason: Score prominence and heading changes do not alter the separate result-driver content or format; the source message's bullet-point refinement is already represented by its own MODIFY.
The front-page score refinement does not change the final-page confidentiality warning; that warning is governed by a separate clause already represented in candidate history.
Renaming and visually emphasizing the score does not change which customer fields must remain editable or the assessment-date field format.
The front-page result-summary changes do not modify internal-page header coverage, content, or presentation; those changes arise from a separate clause in the same message.
Score prominence and heading changes do not affect the vehicle identifier or its display format; the vehicle-section refinement is independently stated and already represented.

The score refinement is a localized front-page requirement and does not necessarily change the existing cross-report visual-theme state; the general design-direction refinement already has its own same-message MODIFY.
The score heading and prominence changes do not alter the DX-17 internal-header identifier, which is established by a separate clause in the source message.
The source Event does not change the assessment-date placeholder policy represented by this Requirement.
The client explicitly says the footer works well, and the front-page score changes do not modify footer presence or content.
Changing the front-page score's prominence and label does not alter the separate scoring table's format or required fields.
The front-page score refinement does not change recommendation content, action orientation, or priority tiers.
The score presentation change does not alter the required DX17–DX20 variant set, editability, or risk-based selection rule.
